name: Years
overview: Scripture reveals that years serve as a divinely appointed measure of time, marked by the sun and moon to distinguish days, seasons, and years, as seen in Genesis 1:14. The early biblical narrative uses years to denote significant life stages and events, such as Adam living 130 years before fathering Seth (Genesis 5:3) and the detailed chronology of the Flood, which began in Noah's 600th year and involved precise counting of days and months (Genesis 7:11, 7:24, 8:3, 8:13). These passages demonstrate that years are foundational to God's ordering of history and human experience, highlighting their importance in understanding redemption, judgment, and divine providence.
